record.original_question: How can one describe all transcendental meromorphic solutions of the difference equation f(z + c1)^2 + f(z + c2)^2 = f(z)^2, where c1 and c2 are fixed distinct nonzero constants?

Open problem 2. How to describe the transcendental meromorphic solutions of the functional equation (3.2) ?
Theorem 3.2. Let f be a transcendental meromorphic (resp. entire) function satisfying (3.2). Then the following situations occur:

(I) If ρ2 (f ) < 1, then f must be of finite order such that f (z) = k1 e^(z log M / c1) F (z) = k2 e^(z log N / c2) G (z), where F and G are meromorphic periodic functions with periods c1 and c2 respectively ... where M, N are distinct and M^2 + N^2 = 1 with k1, k2, M, N ∈ C \ {0}.

(II) If ρ2 (f ) ≥ 1 and, φ(z) and ψ(z) are entire function and meromorphic function respectively such that ψ(z) ≡ k1 ψ (z + c1 ) ≡ k2 ψ (z + c2 ), then f must be of the form f (z) = e^φ(z) ψ(z), where k1, k2 ∈ C \ {0}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ be two fixed distinct nonzero constants. A meromorphic function $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ is called transcendental if it is not a rational function. Recall that the order of $f$ is $\rho(f)=\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log T(r,f)}{\log r}$ and the hyper-order is $\rho_2(f)=\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{\log\log T(r,f)}{\log r}$, where $T(r,f)$ is the Nevanlinna characteristic.

Describe (classify) all transcendental meromorphic functions $f$ on $\mathbb{C}$ that satisfy the difference equation
$$f(z+c_1)^2 + f(z+c_2)^2 = f(z)^2 \qquad (z\in\mathbb{C}).$$

In particular, give a complete characterization of the form of every such transcendental meromorphic (and, separately, every transcendental entire) solution, without restriction on the hyper-order $\rho_2(f)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A partial classification is available: under the additional assumption $\rho_2(f)<1$, every transcendental meromorphic solution must be of finite order and admits an explicit representation $f(z)=k_1 e^{z\log M/c_1}F(z)=k_2 e^{z\log N/c_2}G(z)$ with $F,G$ periodic of periods $c_1,c_2$ and constants satisfying $M^2+N^2=1$. The general case (without the hyper-order restriction) of describing all transcendental meromorphic solutions appears to remain open; related Fermat-type difference equations are an active research area but no complete unconditional classification of this specific equation was located.

status_evidence.title: Transcendental meromorphic solutions of certain nonlinear difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of nonlinear difference equations of Fermat type and their meromorphic solutions using Nevanlinna theory.
status_evidence.claim: Related Fermat-type nonlinear difference equations are studied, but a full unconditional classification for f(z+c1)^2+f(z+c2)^2=f(z)^2 is not established.

status_evidence.title: On entire solutions of some Fermat type differential-difference equations
status_evidence.snippet: Investigations of entire solutions of Fermat-type differential-difference equations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context that Fermat-type difference equations of similar form admit only restricted classes of solutions, typically under finite-order assumptions.
